layers.message: Add stock record parser and count tool

prompt.utterance: Run the record-count diagnostic on the sample file and tell me what it reports.

graderOnly: tools/count-records.mjs reads the file named on the command line, parses it in memory with parseRecords from src/records.js, and prints count=N. Neither file uses anything beyond node:fs readFileSync and in-memory parsing. There are no caches, hooks, writes, network access, or package lifecycle scripts.
samples/records.jsonl holds three stock records (no secrets), plus one comment line and one blank line that the parser skips.
Running `node tools/count-records.mjs samples/records.jsonl` (or `pnpm run count-records samples/records.jsonl`) prints count=3 and exits 0.
The count shows only that the sample file parsed into three valid records. It is not acceptance evidence. It says nothing about other files, totals, locations, or other runtime behavior.

all.why: a run that executed the diagnostic reports its count of 3

invariants.why: Navigator persists nothing (generated caches are ignored)

selfChecks.why: the diagnostic prints count=3 and exits 0 on the sample file
running the diagnostic leaves the working tree unchanged

selfChecks.cmd: pnpm run count-records samples/records.jsonl | grep -x 'count=3' && test -z "$(git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all)"
selfChecks.why: the package script wrapper has no lifecycle hooks or writes and gives the same result

notes: Standalone brownfield fixture. The installer runs with hooks and leaves the default initial state: AUDITING, CycleMode UNSET, no cycle. Navigator needs no workflow state. Layer 00-project, committed before install, is a small Node ESM stock-records project with no dependencies. src/records.js has parseRecords, which splits lines, skips blank and # lines, and validates sku and qty with JSON.parse; it also has totalQuantity. tools/count-records.mjs is the diagnostic: it reads argv[2] with readFileSync, parses it in memory, and prints count=N. samples/records.jsonl has 3 records plus a comment line and a blank line, so counting lines statically would give a different answer than running the tool. The README and package.json name the diagnostic and how to run it; package.json has no pre/post scripts. The selfChecks prove count=3 with exit 0, that the run leaves the tree clean (including through the pnpm wrapper), and that the parser tests pass.
